title: Holy Sheet workbook schema
description: Input format for HolySheet\Agent::write(). Describes a multi-sheet xlsx workbook agentically. Everything in this schema is SUPPORTED NOW: values, formulas, per-column types and number formats, per-cell styling, themes, merges, frozen panes, column widths, totals and comments. A workbook is judged by how it READS, not only by whether the numbers are right — money should render as money and a header row should look like one, so prefer a typed column over a raw number and set the presentation the document needs.

sheets.description: One or more sheets. The first sheet is shown when the file opens.

meta.description: Optional workbook metadata surfaced in Excel's File → Info pane.

name.description: Tab label in Excel. Excel limits to 31 chars and forbids /\?*[]:

columns.description: When present, the first row is the header row. Column types are applied to every row in that column.

items.description: One row of cell values, in column order. Use null for missing values.

cells.description: Sparse cells keyed by A1 address, for anything the row/column model does not cover — a title band, a callout, a note. May be used ALONGSIDE columns/rows: the explicit cell wins at its address and inherits that column's format for anything it does not set.

totals.description: Symbolic aggregations appended below the data. Key = column header; value = one of sum, avg, count, min, max. These become real FORMULAS, so a total updates when a figure above it is edited — a row of typed numbers looks identical and is wrong the moment anyone changes anything.

theme.description: Pre-baked style preset applied to headers, banding and totals. The cheapest way to make a sheet look deliberate: set it unless you are styling every cell yourself.

mergedRegions.description: Cells to merge, as [{start, end}] — e.g. [{"start": "A1", "end": "D1"}]. Use it for a title band spanning the table.

columnWidths.description: Override widths in pixels. Keys are 0-based column indexes. Set these when a header or a formatted number would otherwise be cut off or shown as ####.

frozenRows.description: How many rows stay visible while the sheet scrolls. Set to 1 whenever there is a header row, so the reader can still see what the columns are further down.

frozenCols.description: How many columns stay visible while the sheet scrolls sideways. Set to 1 when the first column is the label for the row.

rowHeights.description: Row heights in pixels, keyed by 1-based row NUMBER as Excel shows it: {"1": 32, "4": 28}. A default row is 20; give a title row or a header row room (28-36) instead of packing text against its fill.

charts.description: Native Excel charts over CELL RANGES on this sheet: edit a figure and the chart follows. Use one whenever the sheet compares values -- a board reader sees the comparison before the numbers. Keep them quiet: a title that states the point, dataLabels with a format, one colour per series.

type.description: column compares categories; bar does it horizontally (long labels, ranked lists); line shows change over time; pie shows parts of ONE whole (at most ~5 slices).

categories.description: The labels along the axis (or the pie's slices), as a range: "A5:A7". Another sheet: "'Data'!A5:A7".

values.description: The numbers, as a range the same length as categories: "B5:B7".

color.description: #RRGGBB. Ignored for a pie, whose slices take a palette.

points.description: Colour single points to make the finding stand out: the one bar or slice the title is about. index is 0-based within values: [{"index": 2, "color": "#C2410C"}].

position.description: Where the chart sits: from its top-left cell to its bottom-right cell, {"from": "E2", "to": "L18"}. Omitted: to the right of the data, 8 columns by 16 rows.

dataLabels.description: Print each value on the chart. Usually right for a board chart.

legend.description: Defaults to on for several series or a pie, off for one series.

format.description: Excel number format for the value axis and labels: "$#,##0", "0.0%", "$#,##0,K".

print.description: How the sheet prints. A sheet wider than a page splits its columns across pages unless fitToWidth is set.

fitToWidth.description: Scale the sheet to one page wide (as many pages tall as it needs).

fitToPage.description: Scale the sheet onto ONE page, wide and tall. Use it for a one-page summary with a chart, so the page break never cuts the chart.

footer.description: A printed footer: up to three slots. {page} and {pages} print the page number and count: {"left": "Q3 Revenue Review", "right": "Page {page} of {pages}"}.

type.description: Cell type applied to every value in this column, and the main thing deciding whether the sheet reads as a document or as a dump. Use 'currency' for money, 'percent' for rates and 'date' for dates — 'auto' infers a plain number and leaves 1250000.5 looking like 1250000.5.

currency.description: ISO currency code for a 'currency' column, e.g. USD. Pair it with decimals: 2.

decimals.description: Decimal places for a numeric, currency or percent column. Money is normally 2; a growth rate is normally 1.

format.description: Custom Excel number format string. Overrides type-derived format. Power-user escape hatch.

width.description: Column width in pixels. Same as columnWidths but per-column.

CellValue.description: A primitive value, null, or an object {value, formula, format, comment} for per-cell control.

computedValue.description: Cached value from a previous evaluation. When present, Excel shows it without recomputing on open.

CellFormat.description: Per-cell presentation: bold, italic, font size, text and background colour, alignment, borders and number format. Use it for the things a column type cannot express — a title band, a highlighted figure, a ruled callout.

CellComment.description: A reviewer note attached to a cell. Accepts a plain string, or an object with text/author/color.

color.description: Hex color for the corner triangle indicator.
